rows: The Flower Grove Co-op Gin reported penny size hail covering Farm to Market 2002 in front of the gin.

Quarter to golfball size hail fell in a swath from northwest of Tarzan to Lenorah. An hour and a half later, an off-duty NWS employee came across drifts of penny to nickel size hail in this same area.
Pea to quarter size hail accumulated to a depth of three to four inches north of Tarzan and Lenorah.
Golfball size hail fell one and a half miles southeast of the intersection of Texas Highway 137 and Farm to Market Road 2002.
Softball size hail fell at the intersection of Texas Highway 349 and Martin County Road D2651.

Just east of Texas Highway 349, nine miles southwest of Patricia, an anticyclonic tornado developed in view of chasers and spotters. Based on the location of the tornado in relation to the supercell, indications are that this tornado developed on the south flank of the rear flank…
Nickel hail fell on Texas Highway 137 north of Lenorah.

The supercell thunderstorm produced another weaker tornado just before 8:30pm CDT. This tornado is believed to have traveled over open country before dissipating east-southeast of the community of Flower Grove.
Penny to nickel size hail was covering Interstate 20 northeast of Stanton.
Quarter to lime sized hail was falling at and just south of the intersection of Farm to Market Road 1212 and Texas Highway 176.
Three to five miles east of the intersection of Texas Highways 349 and 176, 50 to 60 mph wind gusts were estimated. No damage was reported.
Quarter sized hail fell three to five miles east of the intersection of Texas Highways 349 and 176.
Golfball sized hail fell on Farm to Market Road 1212, five to seven miles south of its intersection with Texas Highway 176.
Multiple powerlines were blown down along Farm to Market Road 2002.
The wind gust was reported by a motorist on Texas State Highway 349. No damage was reported.
Baseball sized hail fell at the intersection of Farm to Market Road 26 and Farm to Market Road 2002.
Winds up to 60 mph were estimated by a trained storm spotter. No damage was reported.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail ten miles north of Midand along Texas State Highway 349.
Severe winds were estimated and no damage was reported.

A thunderstorm moved over Martin County and produced a 60 mph wind gust thirteen miles northwest of Tarzan.
A thunderstorm moved over Martin County and produced a 50 to 60 mph wind gust in northeast Martin County.
A thunderstorm moved over Martin County and produced a 50 to 60 mph wind gust in northeast Martin County.
A thunderstorm moved over Martin County and produced wind damage in Lenorah. Part of a roof was blown off of a house. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Martin County and produced a tornado near Patricia. A spotter reported this as a brief rope tornado. No damage was reported or indicated during a storm damage survey, so this tornado was rated as an EF-0. The path length and width were estimated, and t…

A thunderstorm moved across Martin County and produced tennis ball sized hail in Stanton. The only damage that was reported during a damage survey was a few dents on the hood of some cars. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Martin County, and the public estimated a 50 to 60 mph wind gust between 415 and 430 pm CDT. No damage was reported.
A thunderstorm moved across Martin County and produced wind damage in Stanton. There were broken tree limbs and damaged car ports in Stanton. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Martin County and produced an estimated 60 mph wind gust in Stanton. In southwest Stanton, playground equipment was turned over and a roof was removed from part of a house. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Martin County and produced an estimated 60 mph wind gust in Merrick lasting five to ten minutes.

A thunderstorm moved across Martin County and produced wind damage in Stanton. There was a roof partially blown off of a home in Stanton. A large tree was also blown down. The time of damage was estimated from radar. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced golf ball sized hail two miles east of Three Leagues. The wind driven hail broke south facing windows on a home. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Martin County and produced a 69 mph wind gust at the mesonet site near Tarzan.

A thunderstorm moved across Martin County and produced wind damage in Tarzan. There was roof damage to a metal outbuilding. The time was estimated by radar. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Multiple pictures were received from social media of tennis ball-size hail in Stanton. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar.
